title: Passing

A novel organised by the movement of consciousness rather than by chronology: long unbroken passages of thought, time-shifts and repetitions, with the external action reported from inside a single mind. A novel of experiment: broken chronology, several narrators, parody of received styles and typographical play, the parts held together by pattern rather than by plot.

The author's characteristic manner is the short novel of the interior life.

title: Black Thunder

title: Southern Road

title: Not Without Laughter

It is a prose fiction work of 1930 by Langston Hughes; it belongs to The Harlem Renaissance and the New Negro and it is catalogued here under novel of development and the growth story; regional novel and the american local-colour inheritance and the record grades it as major canon and its author standing in the first rank of this corpus.
plot_or_argument: Sandy Rogers grows up in Stanton, Kansas, in the household of his grandmother Aunt Hager, the matriarch of the family, among his aunts Annjee and Harriet and the men who come and go; the novel follows his childhood, his schooling, his work and his departure for the city, in the portrait of a Black family in the Middle West.
narrative_structure: A novel of childhood in chapters, from the porch to the train. A novel in chapters grouped by the stages of a life, from childhood through the education and the first disappointments to the settlement of the adult. A novel in chapters inside one region, the seasons, the trades and the dialect carrying the plot.

title: The Blacker the Berry: A Novel of Negro Life

title: Infants of the Spring

title: Black No More

title: The Conjure-Man Dies: A Mystery Tale of Dark Harlem

Prose of the fair-play mystery: the puzzle is stated in plain narrative prose, the clues are given to the reader as they are given to the investigator, the timetable and the plan are exact, and the solution is delivered in a set-piece explanation. title: The Philosophy and Opinions of Marcus Garvey
